The function `hammingDistance` compares the two-character arrays `s1` and `s2` that are given as arguments. `s1` and `s2` have one or more elements. If `s1` and `s2` do not have the same number of elements, the function returns -1. Otherwise, it returns the number of indices where two arrays have different element values at the same index. The figure shows an example of two character arrays. APPLE and APRIE have different element values at two indices.

Table  Examples of `s1` and `s2` given to the function `hammingDistance` and the return values

○ integer: hammingDistance(character []: s1, character []: s2)
  integer: i, cnt ← 0
  if (the number of elements in s1 ≠ the number of elements in s2)
    return −1
  endif
  for (increase i from 1 to the number of elements in s1 by 1)
    if ([[ ]])
      cnt ← cnt + 1
    endif
  endfor
  return cnt
